89.0.0.en: 1- I will sing of the mercies of the Lord for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.

89.0.1.en: 1- The writer feels that because of the multitude of his sins he needs many mercies from God, and when God declared His mercy to him his mouth was loosed in praise, glorifying God who forgave him; indeed, out of the intensity of his joy he declares that he will keep praising and singing to God for ever, that is, all his life, and from generation to generation, that is, in this life and in the eternal life.

89.0.2.en: 2- After the writer of the Psalm thanked God for His mercies, he also proclaims the truth of God, that is, His justice. God is perfect in His justice, but God's mercy came first in the person of Christ the Redeemer, for He paid the debt on our behalf, had mercy on us, and forgave us our sins.

89.1.0.en: 2- For I have said, “Mercy shall be built up for ever: thy faithfulness shalt thou establish in the very heavens.”

89.1.1.en: 1- This verse is the purpose of the whole Psalm, which is the glorifying of God's mercy that is increasing on the earth, and the children of God feel it piled up, being built and rising higher and higher until it almost reaches heaven. The writer of the Psalm discovered this truth about God's mercy through his life with God; therefore he said, “I have said.”

89.1.2.en: 2- If God's mercy is built up on earth, His truth is firm in heaven, where the angels are subject to Him and praise Him. That is, God has mercy on those on earth and forgives them, so that they may reach heaven and be established in His truth for ever; for people on earth are changeable and liable to fall into error and need God's mercy, but in heaven they are established in the justice of God, His fear and the glorifying of His holy name.

89.1.3.en: 3- God's mercy on His children is built up on earth and rises, and its foundation is God's truth and justice. For He is perfect in His truth and justice, which appeared and were fulfilled in the fullness of time in Christ Jesus.

89.2.0.en: 3- I have made a covenant with my chosen, I have sworn unto David my servant, 4- Thy seed will I establish for ever, and build up thy throne to all generations. Selah.

89.2.1.en: 1- God's mercy appears in its perfection when He makes a covenant with His righteous son David, whom He chose to live with Him and also to make king over His people, and from whose offspring Christ would come. And He directs this covenant of His to every person who believes in Him and lives for Him, so that he becomes chosen by God, and He blesses him for ever, and establishes his throne in heaven, and also blesses his offspring who live as he does with God.

89.2.2.en: 2- These verses apply to David and his offspring, who is Solomon, who sat on his throne after him (2 Sam 7:12-14), and indeed many kings from the offspring of David sat on the throne of the kingdom of Judah, but the carrying out of these verses is completed by Christ, who reigns on the throne of David for ever, and it says “thy seed” and not “thy seeds,” because it means Christ, as St. Paul the Apostle said (Gal 3:16).

89.2.3.en: 3- The kingship of Christ from generation to generation means His reign over the Jews and the Gentiles who believe in Him. And Christ also reigns from generation to generation, that is, over the hearts of His children who are on earth, and then in heaven.

89.2.4.en: 4- These two verses end with the word “Selah,” which is a musical tone for meditating on the mercy of God that appeared in Christ Jesus.

89.3.0.en: 5- And the heavens shall praise thy wonders, O Lord: thy faithfulness also in the congregation of the saints.

89.3.1.en: 1- The heavens are the angels who saw the Incarnation of Christ, and then His Resurrection and redemption, and they praised and glorified Him. The heavens are the Church and the believers on earth who glorify the wondrous works of God and His care for His children. We call the believers on earth heaven because they repent of their sins and accept the commandments of God, and so become sons of heaven, and call God their heavenly Father.

89.3.2.en: 2- The truth of God, that is, His justice, appears in the congregation of the saints who are on earth, for because they held fast to the commandments of God and left evil, He gives them peace and blessing in their lives. And God's truth also appears in the congregation of the saints who have reached heaven, for He compensates them for what they endured on earth with glories in heaven.

89.4.0.en: 6- For who in the heaven can be compared unto the Lord? who among the sons of the mighty can be likened unto the Lord? 7- God is greatly to be feared in the assembly of the saints, and to be had in reverence of all them that are about him.

89.4.1.en: Assembly: gatherings, that is, congregations. God is not only great on earth, but in heaven also, for He is the One who created all the heavenly beings. And there is none like Him in heaven and among the sons of God who are the angels, all of whom are His servants. They are all sons by adoption, but Christ is the only heavenly Son of the Father in essence, and all fear Him, glorify Him and revere Him; all hold Him in awe, and in the assembly of the saints in heaven God is fearful, great and glorified.

89.4.2.en: Meditate on the mercies of God in your life and His longsuffering toward you, so that you may thank Him and praise Him, and your mind will be enlightened and His beauty will be revealed to you, and you will rejoice in Him.

89.5.s.en: (2) The Almighty God, the glory of His people

89.5.0.en: 8- O Lord God of hosts, who is a strong Lord like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?

89.5.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm glorifies God in His power, for there is none like Him in power among all the pagan gods and among all the powers of the world, because He is their Creator. So Miriam the sister of Moses sang before the people of God when they came out of the Red Sea and said, “Who is like unto thee, O Lord” (Ex 15:11), and so the Church praises God every day in the First Hoos with the same words of Miriam.

89.5.2.en: 2- And God, besides His power, is just, and His truth is round about Him, radiating from Him, for He is the source of truth, and it is manifest in His angels who are in heaven and His believing children who are on earth.

89.6.0.en: 9- Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them.

89.6.1.en: 1- The power of God appears in His dominion over the high waves of the sea, and over all its might. This happened when He divided the Red Sea before Moses (Ex 14) and the river Jordan before Joshua (Josh 3:16), and also the Book of Job bore witness to the power of God and His authority over the sea (Job 38:8, 9).

89.6.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about the authority of Christ over the sea when He rebuked the stormy winds and the raging sea, and they obeyed Him and were silent at once (Mk 4:39). The sea signifies the world and its turmoils, that is, God, the Creator of the sea and the world, has authority over all the turmoils of the world and controls them for the sake of His children, for He is the Controller of all.

89.7.0.en: 10- Thou hast broken Rahab in pieces, as one that is slain; thou hast scattered thine enemies with thy strong arm.

89.7.1.en: Rahab: what is meant by it is Egypt, which was a great and dreaded state in ancient times, for it was the first empire that appeared in the world.

89.7.2.en: 1- The power of God appeared in crushing Egypt with all the power of its gods by means of the ten plagues to bring His people out of it, and He even drowned Pharaoh and his army, the greatest army at that time, and freed His people from the bondage of Egypt, and cast the bodies of the Egyptians on the shore of the Red Sea, and by this God scattered His enemies, that is, the enemies of His people, so that they became nothing before the power of God.

89.7.3.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about the crucified Christ, for it said “with thy strong arm,” a reference to His Incarnation, who by His death bound Satan, scattered his power, freed His children who believe in Him, and brought them up from Hades to Paradise.

89.8.0.en: 11- The heavens are thine, the earth also is thine: as for the world and the fulness thereof, thou hast founded them.

89.8.1.en: 12- The north and the south thou hast created them: Tabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name.

89.8.2.en: 1- The heavens that He created belong to God, and they are the angels who praise Him, and likewise the earth in which those who believe in Him dwell and also glorify Him. Indeed all who dwell on earth through the generations and in every place, in the north and the south, and also the east (Hermon) and the west (Tabor): all praise, shout for joy and glorify God.

89.8.3.en: 2- The north may signify what is opposed to God, for from the north came the many attacks on the people of God in ancient times, such as Assyria, Babylon, the Medes and Persia. What is meant is that God is the Creator of all, even those who turn away from Him and are hostile to Him, and He does not allow them to fight His people except to the measure suitable for His people, and He gives His children strength to resist the enemies.

89.9.0.en: 13- Thou hast a mighty arm: strong is thy hand, and high is thy right hand.

89.9.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm glorifies God because He has ability and power over the whole world, and perhaps when he says “arm” and “thy hand” he means the Incarnation of Christ. For Christ, by His redemption, has authority over all, and He also bound the demons.

89.9.2.en: 2- The right hand of God is high, and the right hand signifies glory, so His glory is above all the glories of the world.

89.10.0.en: 14- Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face.

89.10.1.en: 1- God is perfect in His justice and judgment, which is the foundation of His throne, but He is longsuffering, so this justice does not appear in its fullness except on the Day of Judgment. And wise is the one who fears God today, so that he is glorified with God on the Day of Judgment.

89.10.2.en: 2- God's mercy and His faithfulness in His promises go before Him now, and we see them in His care for His children. And they appeared clearly in the New Testament by the redemption of Christ. And whoever benefits from the mercy and the promises of God that go before Him enjoys happiness in the end in eternal life.

89.11.0.en: 15- Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound: they shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance.

89.11.1.en: 1- When those who believe in God saw His wondrous light their hearts were illumined, and they left everything behind to walk in the life of light, that is, by the commandments of God they walked in the way of righteousness, rejoicing in seeing God and His face that looks upon them with His care and love, and He lifts them above all the desires of the world, and they express their joy by shouting and praising His holy name. They behold God because they are pure in heart, and for this the writer of the Psalm calls them blessed, because of their enjoyment of the vision of God and their walking in light.

89.11.2.en: 2- The face of God that shines upon His children appeared clearly in the Incarnation of the only-begotten Son, and those who believed in Him and walked with Him in a life of righteousness enjoyed seeing Him, and shouted joyfully for the new life. They are the blessed Apostles and all the followers of Christ who were discipled at His hands.

89.12.0.en: 16- In thy name shall they rejoice all the day: and in thy righteousness shall they be exalted.

89.12.1.en: 1- Remembering God and repeating His holy name makes a person feel the presence of God and so he rejoices, and continuing to remember the name of God all day gives man constant joy. What is meant by the day is the whole life. As for sin, it gives only a temporary pleasure, and after it sorrow and distress take over.

89.12.2.en: 2- God's justice rewards the righteous who remember His name, so He lifts them in this life above the sin that abases man, then lifts them in heaven and glorifies them and compensates them for all the toils of the earth.

89.13.0.en: (17- For thou art the glory of their strength: and in thy favour our horn shall be exalted. 18- For the Lord is our defence; and the Holy One of Israel is our king.

89.13.1.en: Our shield: the shield is the large buckler, a defensive instrument consisting of a large piece of wood with a handle at the back in which the soldier puts his hand, and he moves it in front of his face and body to ward off arrows.

89.13.2.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm here shows the reason for the exaltation of the children of God mentioned in the previous verse, saying: because God is the cause of the strength of His children, in which they glory, and indeed when they walk in His commandments they obtain His favour, so their horn is exalted, that is, their strength appears, which frightens their enemies the demons.

89.13.3.en: 2- Also God is the shield, that is, the defender of His righteous children, and more than this, God the Holy One, the God of Israel, is the One who reigns over the hearts of His children and keeps them from every evil, so that no one can harm them, that is, He keeps them in righteousness and holiness, enjoying His fellowship, rejoicing at all times.

89.13.4.en: Your God is strong above all the powers of the world, so hold fast to His commandments, take care to please Him, and remember His name at all times, and God will rejoice in you and protect you, and your heart will rejoice.

89.14.s.en: (3) The promises of God to David and his seed

89.14.0.en: 19- Then thou spakest in vision to thy holy one, and saidst, I have laid help upon one that is mighty; I have exalted one chosen out of the people. 20- I have found David my servant; with my holy oil have I anointed him: 21- With whom my hand shall be established: mine arm also shall strengthen him.

89.14.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm speaks in these verses about David the prophet and king, to whom Nathan the prophet spoke in a vision (1 Chr 17:15) concerning the building of the house of God, which David wished to do. And God said to him that his son would be the one to build the house, and God gave strength and help to David the strong and great, so he increased in strength upon strength, and He chose him from among all the children of Israel to anoint him king, and established his kingdom, so he triumphed over all the surrounding enemies, and God quelled the revolt of Absalom, and kept David all the days of his life because he was righteous and his heart was like the heart of God.

89.14.2.en: 2- These verses are also a prophecy about Christ the only-begotten Son, who became incarnate and was the second Adam, and the perfect man who feared God in His conduct, so He did not sin in anything, and the Father upheld Him by the Holy Spirit and chose Him from among all mankind, and anointed Him with the Holy Spirit when He was baptized in the Jordan, and He triumphed over all the devices of Satan in the temptation on the mountain, and in the Jews' opposition to Him, and then completed His victory in the redemption of mankind on the Cross and bound Satan.

89.15.0.en: 22- The enemy shall not exact upon him; nor the son of wickedness afflict him.

89.15.2.en: 1- As for the enemies, none of them was able to compel David, or seize him, humiliate him, and force him to any evil deed, but on the contrary God was protecting him from the pursuit of Saul, and likewise Absalom, and in the end God crushed his enemies, so Saul died in the war, and Absalom also. And David triumphed over his enemies in the surrounding lands, so they submitted to him and offered him gifts. As for Saul, he fell into David's hand twice and David forgave him, but David never fell into anyone's hand.

89.15.3.en: 2- All of the above happened with Christ, who proclaimed the truth everywhere, and Satan could not humiliate Him, but on the contrary He said to the crowds, “Which of you convinceth me of sin?” (Jn 8:46). And in the end Christ bound Satan at His death on the Cross

89.16.0.en: 24- But my faithfulness and my mercy shall be with him: and in my name shall his horn be exalted.

89.16.1.en: 1- God speaks and says that He takes care of David with all faithfulness and fulfills the promises to him, and has mercy on him, so He forgives him all his sins. Then in the name and power of God, David is strengthened, and he expresses this strength by the raising and exalting of his horn.

89.16.2.en: 2- The Father gave all authority to the Son in faithfulness, and mercy was completed in Christ who redeemed the world. And in His holy name His horn was exalted when He defeated the demons and bound them by His Cross.

89.17.0.en: 25- I will set his hand also in the sea, and his right hand in the rivers.

89.17.1.en: 1- David's authority extended over the sea and over the rivers, for he triumphed over all the surrounding enemies and subdued them to himself. The sea signifies the world, that is, the pagans, and the rivers signify the believers, so David had authority over his people, that is, the rivers, and over the surrounding nations, that is, the sea.

89.17.2.en: 2- Christ had authority over the sea and the rivers, that is, the Gentiles and the Jews, and He spoke as one having authority and not as the scribes and Pharisees, and after His Resurrection and Ascension believers of Gentile and Jewish origin believed in Him.

89.18.0.en: 26- He shall cry unto me, Thou art my father, my God, and the rock of my salvation. 27- Also I will make him my firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth.

89.18.1.en: 1- God showed His love and fatherhood to David, so that David said in the second Psalm, “The Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee” (Ps 2:7). And David also felt the power of God supporting him, so he called Him “the rock of my salvation,” and God chose David from among his brothers, and gave him the blessing of the birthright when he anointed him king in his father's house by the hand of Samuel, and he became firstborn in his relationship with God, so that God testified that his heart was like the heart of God (Acts 13:22).

89.18.2.en: 2- These two verses are a prophecy about Christ the only-begotten Son, who called God His Father sixty times in the Holy Bible. And Christ, in respect of His humanity, calls God the rock of His salvation, that is, His strength, and He is of course the firstborn among many brethren, for He is the firstfruits of those who slept, who rose from the dead to raise by His Resurrection those who believe in Him.

89.19.0.en: 28- My mercy will I keep for him for evermore, and my covenant shall stand fast with him. 29- His seed also will I make to endure for ever, and his throne as the days of heaven.

89.19.1.en: 1- God's mercy keeps and forgives David and his seed for ever, as long as they walk in righteousness like their father David. And God establishes His covenant with them by caring for them and saving them, and the days of David's seed before God are like the duration of the heavens, that is, unshakable. And the seed of David is not only those who reigned over the tribe of Judah, but even more it is fulfilled in Christ the Son of David who reigns for ever.

89.19.2.en: 2- If we apply these two verses to Christ as a prophecy about Him, then God's mercy and covenant are for ever, because He is God who reigns for ever. And the divine mercy appears to the seed of Christ, that is, those who believe in His name, who are the Church His Body, so God has mercy on them and cares for them with His care, not only on earth but for ever in the heavens.

89.20.0.en: 30- If his children forsake my law, and walk not in my judgments; 31- If they break my statutes, and keep not my commandments; 32- Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with stripes.

89.20.1.en: The justice of God with His children appears, whether the seed of David or those who believe in Christ, for He does not show partiality to them if they sin by leaving His commandments and teachings, and likewise the ordinances and rites of His worship, but disciplines them with a rod and stripes, that they may repent and return to Him, and that they may know that when sin is committed He forsakes them, so they face problems that perhaps they may return to Him.

89.21.0.en: 33- Nevertheless my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him, nor suffer my faithfulness to fail. 34- My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips. 35- Once have I sworn by my holiness that I will not lie unto David.

89.21.1.en: God's mercy remains upon the seed of David and those who believe in Christ because He wants their salvation even if He has to use discipline. God remains faithful in His promises to David and His mercy to his seed, for God is unchanging, with Him there is no variation, so He does not break His promises in caring for His people. If they sin He is longsuffering toward them, for He kept the seed of David as kings over the kingdom of Judah even the wicked among them. For God swore that the seed of David would remain kings for ever, and this was fulfilled in Christ. As for the wicked seed of David who persisted in being far from God, God punished them with eternal destruction.

89.22.0.en: 36- His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun before me. 37- It shall be established for ever as the moon, and as a faithful witness in heaven. Selah.

89.22.1.en: 1- The faithfulness of God is fulfilled in His promises to David to establish his kingdom as the sun and moon are fixed in nature. And in heaven Christ, who is of the seed of David, reigns for ever over the hearts of His children, and all the seed of David who believe in God reign with Him, and they are witnesses to the truth of God's promises.

89.22.2.en: 2- This passage ends with the word “Selah,” which is a musical pause for meditating on the love of God and His care for His children.

89.22.3.en: Trust in the promises of God and His fatherhood, which cares for you even if you are weak and fall into sin, for He is longsuffering toward you. He may discipline you and forsake you for a short time, then return and forgive you and compensate you for what has passed. [4] The annulling of God's promises (vv. 38 - 45)

89.23.0.en: (38- But thou hast cast off and abhorred, thou hast been wroth with thine anointed. 39- Thou hast made void the covenant of thy servant: thou hast profaned his crown by casting it to the ground.

89.23.1.en: 1- God gave great promises to David and his seed, but the condition for the continuance of these promises was holding fast to a life of righteousness, otherwise God is ready to break His covenant. This is what actually happened in the days of David, when his son Absalom rose against him and drove him from the kingdom, and David went out running barefoot in humiliation. And people asked why God rejected David the Lord's anointed, that is, the one anointed king by Him? And why was his crown profaned, that is, why was he removed as king from his throne? And the reason of course is God's discipline so that David's repentance for his sin with the wife of Uriah the Hittite might be realized.

89.23.2.en: 2- God's rejection of His anointed was carried out in His rejection of the seed of David who sinned, such as Rehoboam, in whose days the kingdom was split, and the Jews almost killed him, so he fled from them. And this was repeated with many kings because of their sins.

89.23.3.en: 3- The rejection of the Lord's anointed was carried out in the greatest person of the seed of David, the Lord Jesus Christ, whom the Jews arrested, despised, scourged and tortured, and then in the end crucified to die. And He endured all this for the sins of all mankind, but He was able to rise from the dead to raise all His children who believe in Him

89.24.0.en: (40- Thou hast broken down all his hedges; thou hast brought his strong holds to ruin. 41- All that pass by the way spoil him: he is a reproach to his neighbours. 42- Thou hast set up the right hand of his adversaries; thou hast made all his enemies to rejoice.

89.24.1.en: 1- This Psalm continues its reproach of God for rejecting His anointed, saying to Him: why did You leave the enemies of Your anointed to tear down the walls of his houses? And even his strongholds have become ruins, and also the neighbors of Your anointed have mocked him and he has become a shame to them, and has shared with the enemies in the ruin of his country. And at the time when You rejected Your anointed You raised up his oppressors and enemies, and they rejoiced in the ruin of his cities. This happened many times with the seed of David, when Assyria, Aram and Babylon attacked him, but the ruin was completed for Jerusalem and its temple at the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, and the Babylonian captivity took place, beginning in the year 605 B.C.

89.24.2.en: 2- These three verses were a prophecy about what happened with Christ when they tore down His body, and His glory, and humiliated Him on the Cross. And His enemies mocked Him. And He endured all these pains for our salvation

89.25.0.en: 43- Thou hast also turned the edge of his sword, and hast not made him to stand in the battle.

89.25.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm reproaches God because He forsook His people, so He was no longer a strength against their enemies, that is, they lost the power of their weapon, which is the sword, and did not triumph. All this of course is because the people turned away from God and worshiped idols.

89.25.2.en: 2- This verse also applies to Christ, for the sword of Christ is His word, which was no longer effective on the people, who rejected His word, and even asked Pilate to crucify Him. And Christ did not fulfill the wishes of the Jews that He become king over them and free them from the Romans, but on the contrary was crucified in humiliation and shame, for they did not understand that He came to reign over them spiritually and to free them from the death of sin.

89.26.0.en: 44- Thou hast made his glory to cease, and cast his throne down to the ground.

89.26.1.en: 1- The glory of the Jews departed and they lost their kingdom when they went into the Assyrian captivity, then the Babylonian, and became humiliated slaves, and this was to discipline them that they might repent.

89.26.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ who lost His glory, that is, His earthly glory, by the Crucifixion, and did not reign as an earthly king over the Jews.

89.26.3.en: 3- With the coming of Christ the Jews lost their glory in respect of the Law and circumcision, which were a type of the New Testament, and they were no longer the chosen people of God, and they lost their dominion and distinction by their refusal to believe in Christ.

89.27.0.en: 45- The days of his youth hast thou shortened: thou hast covered him with shame. Selah.

89.27.1.en: 1- This verse applies to the kingdom of Judah, which lost its strength and vitality, that is, its youth, through the Babylonian captivity, after the kingdom of Israel its sister lost its strength and youth through the Assyrian captivity, and it was covered with shame by the bondage of captivity.

89.27.2.en: 2- This verse also applies to Christ, who died young on the Cross, and was covered with shame and disgrace before men, but in truth by His death He trampled death.

89.27.3.en: 3- This verse was fulfilled in one of the stages of the Babylonian captivity on King Jehoiachin, who was young in age, who reigned only three months, then was taken captive to Babylon, that is, shame covered him, but after he had been imprisoned for a long time the king of Babylon returned and freed him and seated him at his table.

89.27.4.en: 4- This verse ends with the word “Selah,” which is a musical tone for meditating during it on God's discipline of us so that we may repent and return to Him.

89.27.5.en: God seeks your salvation by every means; if He allows you a trial, trust that He loves you and wants your repentance so that you may obtain your salvation, and then He gives you the joy of fellowship with Him and you rejoice with Him on earth, and then in eternity.

89.27.6.en: [5] Pleading for the mercies of God (vv. 46 - 52):

89.28.0.en: 46- How long, Lord? wilt thou hide thyself for ever? shall thy wrath burn like fire? The writer of the Psalm felt that God's wrath and discipline had lasted long upon his people, so he pleads with God to stop this wrath, for the people know their sin and will repent, but God of course knows when the repentance of His people will be complete, and then He will lift His wrath and bring them back from captivity with great honor.

89.29.0.en: 47- Remember how short my time is: wherefore hast thou made all men in vain? 48- What man is he that liveth, and shall not see death? shall he deliver his soul from the hand of the grave? Selah.

89.29.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm reminds God that the life of man on earth is short. He is passing and vain, that is, he does not remain on earth for ever. All mankind will die and go to Hades (the grave), because redemption has not yet been accomplished, and therefore he pleads with God to lift His discipline, so that they may rest a little before their lives end in the bondage of captivity and humiliation.

89.29.2.en: 2- These two verses end with the word “Selah,” which is a musical tone during which man meditates on how he is a stranger on earth, and sees that his only hope is God, so he prays, and his heart clings to Him.

89.30.0.en: 49- Lord, where are thy former lovingkindnesses, which thou swarest unto David in thy truth? 50- Remember, Lord, the reproach of thy servants; how I do bear in my bosom the reproach of all the mighty people; 51- Wherewith thine enemies have reproached, O Lord; wherewith they have reproached the footsteps of thine anointed.

89.30.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm asks God about His promises to David and his seed of many mercies; for if the people had sinned, the divine discipline is enough, and they have repented and need the mercy of God, especially since the people of God have borne much reproach within them from the pagan nations, that is, Assyria and Babylon which humiliated them. So he pleads with God to lift from them this shame and humiliation, which befell the seed of David, that is, the footsteps of His anointed; for David is the Lord's anointed and his footsteps are his offspring.

89.30.2.en: 2- The fatherhood of the writer of the Psalm and his love for his people appear, for he feels that the shame, disgrace and sufferings of the people of God have come upon him, indeed he carries them in his bosom and suffers for them; therefore his prayers rose in this Psalm that God might stop His wrath and have mercy on His people.

89.30.3.en: 3- These verses apply to Christ, who cries out to the Father that the cup of sufferings, the sufferings of the Cross, pass from Him, because He bore in His bosom all the sufferings of mankind and its sins, and bore the shame of the Cross; for Christ is the seed of David, that is, the footsteps of His anointed. For David is the Lord's anointed, and Jesus Christ is the footsteps of David who bore all the shame and redeemed His people.

89.30.4.en: 4- The footsteps of Christ are the believers in Christ who endure the wars of the demons and the shame of humiliation for the sake of Christ, and ask God to lift from them trials and afflictions, and He gives them His mercies which He promised His children.

89.31.0.en: 52- Blessed be the Lord for evermore. Amen, and Amen. He ends the Psalm with this verse that glorifies God, for He deserves blessing and honor for ever; because this ending is not only the end of this Psalm, but the end of the third part of the Psalms according to the division of the Jews, for the Jews divide the Psalms into five books, and Psalm 89 is the end of the third book, and it is noticed that this verse is repeated at the close of the first four books only.

89.31.1.en: Your repentance and your humility before God every day open for you the door of God's mercies so that they flow over you; for God is compassionate and gives generously to the humble who ascribe the glory to Him, and thus you live reassured, and walk with wide steps in the way of the Kingdom.

89.31.2.en: Asceticism is the way to the knowledge of God. A prayer of Moses the man of God. “Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations ...” (v. 1). Introduction:

89.31.3.en: 1- Its writer is Moses the prophet, as is mentioned in the title of the Psalm, and the similarity is noticed between this Psalm and the Book of Deuteronomy which Moses the prophet wrote, especially the Song of Moses (Deut 32). And the title mentions that Moses is the man of God, and this description is mentioned more than 4 times in the Holy Bible for godly men of God.

89.31.4.en: 2- When was it written? Most likely Moses wrote it in the wilderness of Sinai after the exodus from the land of Egypt, when he was angry with his people who murmured against him, who wanted to return to Egypt, refusing to enter the land of Canaan, so He made them wander in the wilderness forty years until they died, and their sons entered the Promised Land, as God's anger appears in (v. 7).

89.31.5.en: 3- This Psalm speaks about asceticism in worldly matters, and leaving the cares of the world so that man may live with God.

89.31.6.en: 4- This Psalm speaks about God's creation of man, then his fall, then his hope of rising from this fall, which will be accomplished by Christ who rose from the dead.

89.31.7.en: 5- This Psalm is the beginning of the fourth section, that is, the fourth book according to the Jews, which begins with Psalm 90 and ends with Psalm 106.

89.31.8.en: 6- This Psalm is not found in the Agpeya.
